title: What to Do If a Bison Charges You: It Can Run 3x Faster Than Humans 🦬 (Would Meatball Survive? #5)
description:
What to do if a bison charges you? Yellowstone's safety page (U.S. National Park Service) says: do not stand your ground. Immediately walk or run away from the animal. If the bison follows you, it says to spray bear spray as you are moving away and seek cover behind nearby trees or cars. The same page says to keep at least 25 yards (23 meters) from bison at all times and never approach a bison to take a photo. It says bison can run 3x faster than humans, and that they have injured more people in Yellowstone than any other animal. If approached too closely, it says, a bison may respond by bluff charging, head bobbing while staring at you, pawing, bellowing, or raising its tail: warning signs that you are too close and that a charge is imminent.

#bison #yellowstone #meatballmyths #shorts

Sources: U.S. National Park Service, Yellowstone National Park (Safety page, updated July 28, 2026). General information, not safety training.
